cards.front: WHO recommends exclusive breastfeeding for the first 6 months and continued breastfeeding with complementary foods until at least [___].
cards.context:
The benefit is dose-dependent: longer exclusive breastfeeding means lower infant mortality, fewer episodes of gastroenteritis and otitis media, less atopy and obesity, and better cognitive outcomes.

Mothers gain reduced breast and ovarian cancer risk.

Australian uptake falls off fast — ~60% exclusive at discharge but only ~25% by 6 months, driven by return-to-work pressure, formula marketing, and unsupported lactation.

cards.front: In pregnancy, systolic BP ≥160 mmHg with diastolic BP below 110 mmHg still meets the threshold for [___].
cards.context: NSW ACI 2026: either component can establish severe hypertension. Do not dismiss a severe systolic value because the diastolic value is lower.

cards.front: PCOS is diagnosed in an adult by two of three features: ovulatory dysfunction, [___] (clinical or biochemical), and polycystic ovarian morphology on ultrasound or a raised AMH.
cards.context:
Polycystic morphology is 20 or more follicles per ovary and/or an ovarian volume of 10 mL or more. AMH may replace ultrasound in adults; neither is used within 8 years of menarche.

Downstream risks: endometrial hyperplasia + cancer from unopposed estrogen (cyclic progestogen if anovulatory), insulin resistance + T2DM, CV disease, and subfertility (letrozole first-line).

Screen glycaemia at diagnosis and every 1-3 years; a 75 g OGTT is the most accurate test.

cards.front: Planned vaginal breech birth is contraindicated when the estimated fetal weight exceeds [___].
cards.context:
The same list treats growth restriction below the 10th centile as a contraindication, not only a large baby.

Cord presentation, a hyperextended neck, and antenatal fetal compromise are also exclusions.

A planned vaginal birth is considered only for a frank or complete breech, and induction is not recommended.

cards.front: Two days after a vaginal birth, a woman has fever 39.5 °C, lower abdominal pain far worse than her mildly tender uterus explains, and BP 84/48 mmHg. There is no rash. The likely toxin-producing organism is [___].
cards.context:
Toxic shock with pain far beyond the examination findings and no rash, after birth or surgery, points to group A streptococcus. Staphylococcal toxic shock, classically menstrual, usually brings a diffuse erythroderma.

Puerperal group A streptococcal sepsis worsens over hours. Treat septic shock at once, adding clindamycin to suppress toxin production, and look for the source.

cards.front: A suspected breech in the late third trimester is confirmed, and a predisposing finding is sought, by [___].
cards.context:
Palpation can be wrong, so the scan confirms what is presenting before version or birth is discussed.

It looks for a fetal anomaly or an undiagnosed placenta praevia, and it measures growth and liquor.

It also looks for neck hyperextension, which changes whether a vaginal breech birth can be planned.

cards.front: In birth suite, a woman receiving magnesium sulfate develops absent patellar reflexes and shallow breathing at 8/min. The obstetric registrar stops the infusion and starts airway support. The specific intravenous antidote is [___].
cards.context:
Absent reflexes with respiratory depression indicate clinically significant magnesium toxicity rather than the brisk reflexes of cerebral irritability.

Calcium antagonises magnesium’s neuromuscular effects. Stopping the infusion and supporting ventilation remain essential while the antidote is prepared.

cards.front: During suckling, milk let-down is driven by [___].
cards.context:
Suckling releases this posterior pituitary hormone, which contracts the myoepithelial cells around the alveoli. Prolactin, from the anterior pituitary, drives milk production instead.

Pain and stress inhibit let-down; the same hormone contracts the uterus, which causes afterpains during feeds.

cards.front: At elective caesarean, the WNHS slow IV oxytocin bolus is [___], followed by an infusion.
cards.context: The caesarean protocol uses smaller slow IV boluses because rapid oxytocin can cause cardiovascular effects. The regimen is agreed between the anaesthetist and obstetrician.

cards.front: A positive hepatitis B surface antigen in a pregnant woman indicates [___] infection.
cards.context:
HBsAg is a viral coat protein made by infected liver cells, so its presence means the woman has hepatitis B now, acute or chronic.

Every pregnant woman is offered HBsAg testing at the first antenatal visit, because her baby can be protected at birth.

cards.front: Mastitis treatment: continue breastfeeding from affected side + flucloxacillin for Staph aureus coverage; abscess if [___] mass develops.
cards.context:
Mastitis is breast inflammation, usually from milk stasis, that can progress to bacterial infection, almost always Staph aureus.

Antibiotics when infection is suspected or it does not settle in 12-24 hours: flucloxacillin 500 mg QID for 5-7 days. Analgesia and cold packs.

Distinguish from engorgement (bilateral, no fever) and cracked nipples alone (visible cracks, painful latch).

cards.front: In antepartum haemorrhage, NEVER perform digital vaginal exam until [___] is excluded by ultrasound; speculum is safe but VE risks catastrophic bleeding.
cards.context:
A finger through the cervical os of a placenta praevia can shear the placental edge directly → catastrophic haemorrhage within seconds.

Workup: maternal history + vitals → speculum to visualise cervix + bleeding source (safe — doesn't enter os) → transabdominal USS to localise placenta.

cards.front: A growth-restricted fetus has slowing abdominal growth but relatively preserved head growth. Doppler shows falling middle cerebral artery resistance despite increasing placental resistance. This compensatory circulatory pattern is [___].
cards.context:
Cerebral vasodilation redirects cardiac output towards vital organs during chronic hypoxaemia. Reduced abdominal growth reflects the same redistribution.

A reassuring head size does not mean placental function is normal. The term describes compensation, not protection from all injury.

cards.front: Before an instrumental birth the bladder is emptied, if needed by in/out [___].
cards.context: A full bladder obstructs descent and is at risk of trauma, so it is emptied first, with an in/out catheter if needed.

cards.front: After the initial steps, start positive-pressure ventilation if the newborn is apnoeic or gasping or the heart rate is below [___].
cards.context:
Ventilation comes first because most neonatal arrests are respiratory in origin. First 30 sec: dry, stimulate, keep warm, position airway; then reassess breathing and HR.

After 30 sec PPV: HR rising + breathing improving → continue support and wean; HR remains <100 → optimise ventilation (MR SOPA); HR <60 despite effective ventilation → add chest compressions 3:1 with breaths.

cards.front: Initial drug treatment of PPH uses oxytocin as a uterotonic plus early [___] 1 g IV as an antifibrinolytic adjunct; avoid ergometrine in HTN and carboprost in asthma.
cards.context:
Treat PPH concurrently: start uterine massage and an appropriate uterotonic such as oxytocin, and give tranexamic acid 1 g IV as soon as possible and within 3 hours of birth.

Tranexamic acid is an antifibrinolytic adjunct, not a uterotonic; a second 1 g dose may be given after 30 minutes if bleeding persists under the protocol.

Escalate uterotonics per protocol. Avoid ergometrine in hypertension or pre-eclampsia and carboprost in asthma.

cards.front: After an instrumental birth, the minimum surveillance schedule includes another structured head assessment at [___].
cards.context:
The same minimum applies after a second-stage caesarean, including babies who look well.

Boggy swelling or a rising circumference moves the baby off that minimum. Leaving the head uncovered is how the change is seen.

cards.front: For syphilis in pregnancy, the only treatment that reliably treats the fetus is [___], so allergic women are desensitised rather than switched.
cards.context:
Alternatives used outside pregnancy are unsuitable: doxycycline is contraindicated, and macrolides do not reliably cross the placenta to treat the fetus.

Women with a true penicillin allergy are referred for supervised desensitisation, then given penicillin.

cards.front: The classic triad of ruptured ectopic pregnancy is [___], vaginal bleeding, and unilateral pelvic pain.
cards.context:
The classic triad occurs in only about half of ectopic pregnancies; presentations may include GI symptoms, shoulder-tip pain or syncope.

Risk rises after previous ectopic, tubal damage or surgery, IVF, or pregnancy with an IUD in situ. Assess with TVUS and serial βhCG; an empty uterus above the local threshold is concerning but not diagnostic.

Rupture with instability needs urgent surgery. Stable, eligible patients with low βhCG and no fetal cardiac activity may be considered for methotrexate.

cards.front: In placental abruption, visible bleeding may [___] reflect severity; concealed abruption can cause DIC and fetal death with minimal external loss.
cards.context:
In abruption, blood may dissect between the placenta and uterine wall WITHOUT escaping through the cervix — concealed haemorrhage.

The concealed component drives DIC: thromboplastin from the disrupted placenta enters maternal circulation, triggering consumption coagulopathy, and the trapped retroplacental clot extends the disruption further.

cards.front: A girl born by breech at 38 weeks has stable hips on Barlow and Ortolani testing at birth and at her 6-week check. She should still have hip [___] at about 6 weeks.
cards.context:
Breech presentation is an indication for imaging on its own. A normal Barlow and Ortolani examination does not exclude a dysplastic acetabulum.

Ultrasound is used because the femoral head is still cartilage; plain X-ray becomes useful only after about 4-6 months.

cards.front: Overflow incontinence is caused by outlet blockage or a weak [___].
cards.context:
Urine leaks because the bladder has been stretched until pressure exceeds urethral pressure. There is no cough and no sudden urge.

Outlet blockage and a detrusor that does not contract are the two routes to that overfilling.

cards.front: For stress incontinence, first-line conservative management is supervised [___] for at least 3 months before reassessment.
cards.context:
PFMT is first-line conservative therapy for stress urinary incontinence; bladder training leads for pure urge/urgency incontinence, with PFMT as an adjunct.

In SUI, stronger levator ani support lifts the bladder neck and improves urethral closure during exertion.

Supervised PFMT needs at least 3 months for strength gains; 60-70% of women improve enough to avoid drug adverse effects or surgery.

cards.front: Non-invasive prenatal testing (NIPT) is a screening test analysing cell-free fetal DNA from 10 weeks; positive results require invasive [___] confirmation.
cards.context:
NIPT analyses cell-free fetal DNA fragments shed by placental trophoblast into maternal blood. The 10-week floor is when fetal fraction is high enough to call reliably; earlier risks an uninterpretable 'no result'.

It is a SCREENING test, not diagnostic — the DNA is placental, not directly fetal, so a positive can be confined placental mosaicism, a vanishing twin, or maternal mosaicism.

That is why a positive must be confirmed by an invasive karyotype (CVS or amniocentesis) before any irreversible decision.
